note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Screens that mix a terminal and a portal carry the second half in also[] (when = before/after the main part). Scenes read MG_LAB_ADMIN_UPN / MG_LAB_DOMAIN (set by prepare, derived from the signed-in labadmin).
prepare: Connect-MgGraph -Scopes User.Read -NoWelcome  # owner signs in (browser); only to read the labadmin address
# seeded leaks use reserved example addresses only; nothing is ever delivered

try { New-InboxRule -Mailbox "taylor.demo@$env:MG_LAB_DOMAIN" -Name 'MG Lab forward' -ForwardTo 'taylor.private@example.com' -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null } catch { Write-Warning "Inbox rule refused: $($_.Exception.Message). Create it in Outlook on the web as taylor.demo (Settings > Mail > Rules) or skip that beat." }

if (-not (Get-TransportRule -Identity 'MG Lab test copy' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { New-TransportRule -Name 'MG Lab test copy' -From "sam.demo@$env:MG_LAB_DOMAIN" -BlindCopyTo 'counsel@example.org' -Mode Audit -Enabled $false | Out-Null }   # no comment on purpose, left disabled

[pscustomobject]@{ removeExtra = $false; mailboxes = @([pscustomobject]@{ alias = 'mglab-support'; displayName = 'MG Lab Support'; fullAccess = @("sam.demo@$env:MG_LAB_DOMAIN"); sendAs = @("sam.demo@$env:MG_LAB_DOMAIN") }) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6 | Set-Content ./src/shared-mailboxes.lab.json
./src/Invoke-ExchangeAdmin.ps1 -SaveSnapshot ./src/snapshot.lab.json -OutFile ./src/audit.lab.md   # off-camera baseline: any CollectionError row must be fixed, not recorded around

screens.name: fix

steps: Between the Fix and the Restore: Exchange admin center > Recipients > Mailboxes > riley.demo > Manage email forwarding: forwarding is off
After the Restore: refresh, forwarding is back on
Show rollback.lab.json with the mailbox address masked

screens.note: The Fix plan covers every mailbox with external forwarding that is not in forwarding.ignoreMailboxes; only riley.demo is seeded. If another mailbox shows up in the -WhatIf plan, it is a real finding: stop and add it to forwarding.ignoreMailboxes in exchange.lab.json before the confirmed run.

steps: Outlook on the web as sam.demo: open the shared mailbox 'MG Lab Support' (right-click the folder list > Add shared folder or mailbox, or wait for auto-mapping)
New message from the shared mailbox to alex.demo, Send
Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > MG Lab Support > Block sign-in
Re-run the audit in the terminal: the SharedMailboxSignInEnabled finding is gone

teardown: Get-InboxRule -Mailbox "taylor.demo@$env:MG_LAB_DOMAIN" | Where-Object Name -eq 'MG Lab forward' | Remove-InboxRule -Confirm:$false
needs: wait:message trace data after the shared-mailbox message can take minutes
